title: Another family pleads against convicted murderer's release - NewsBreak
text:
By Abigail Franklin ,
1 days ago
OKLAHOMA CITY ( KFOR ) — The Zacarias family is sharing their outrage over the potential release of a woman involved in their father’s murder.
It’s been nearly 50 years since six employees at an Oklahoma City Sirloin Stockade restaurant were forced into a walk-in freezer and executed.
Family speaks out to keep convicted murderer behind bars. Image: Elizabeth Payne. “A very, very hard day. Very hard day,” said Marth Zacarias, whose father was killed in the Sirloin Stockade murders.
Martha Zacarias is the daughter of Louis Zacarias.
Brent Swadley rushed to ER after jail incident, attorney says Another family pleads against convicted murderer’s release. Image: Martha Zacarias. He was murdered by Roger and Verna Stafford in 1978 while he was working at the Sirloin Stockade restaurant, along with five others.
The couple is also responsible for the murder of the Lorenz family just weeks before the mass murder.
“I was 18 years old when he was killed, and I had just gotten married,” said Zacarias. “It was supposed to be a wonderful time growing up and being able to have my daddy, my husband, my family. He was a very young entrepreneur. You know, Made it all the way. Fought and clawed and made his business successful.”
In 1995, Roger was executed. Verna is still alive and serving out two consecutive life sentences since 1980.
“I want Oklahomans to remember that day, to remember the Steak House murders, to remember the cruelty with which they were murdered, shot, execution style inside the meat locker,” said Zacarias.
The Pardon and Parole Board confirmed to News 4 that Verna passed stage one of the parole process.
“I’m afraid that it would set a lot of people back emotionally, mentally,” said Zacarias.
News 4 sat down with former District Attorney Andy Coats in 2006, who said Verna cooperated in the case.
“I did think she deserved some kind of break in terms of the length of the sentence,” said Coats in 2006. “I did not contemplate that she’d be in prison for the rest of her life.”
He assumed Verna would spend less than 10 years in prison after she testified against her husband.
“She has certainly paid for her participation, which in my job was somewhat limited in this terrible crime,” said Coats in 2006.
Martha Zacarias says Verna needs to stay in prison.
“All the victims are serving the life sentences,” said Zacarias. “She was given two life sentences plus 999 years, and we, as the families, have continued to serve that life sentence.”
Verna has applied for parole several times. She is expected to have a hearing in August.
The family is encouraging people to write letters to the governor’s office with their opinions.
